rubric.why: Valency is an atom’s combining capacity.
rubric.description: Defines valency as the combining capacity of an atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that valency is an atom’s combining capacity.

rubric.why: A radical is a charged atom or group of atoms that acts as one unit.
rubric.description: Defines a radical as a charged atom or group of atoms acting as a single unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a radical as a charged atom or group of atoms behaving as one unit.

modelAnswer: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom.
A radical is an atom or group of atoms carrying a positive or negative charge and behaving as a single unit in chemical reactions.

items.followUp: Write two differences between a molecule and an ion.

rubric.why: An atom has no net electrical charge, whereas an ion is charged.
rubric.description: States that an atom is electrically neutral and an ion carries a charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the electrical charges of atoms and ions.

rubric.why: Atoms have equal numbers of protons and electrons; ions form when electrons are lost or gained.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid difference based on electron count or ion formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms have equal numbers of protons and electrons, or that ions form by loss or gain of electrons.

modelAnswer: An atom is electrically neutral, whereas an ion has a positive or negative charge.
An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons; an ion forms when an atom loses or gains electrons.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of an atom having 12 electrons.

rubric.why: Electronic configuration describes how electrons are distributed among shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the arrangement or distribution of electrons.

rubric.why: The electrons are arranged in shells around the nucleus.
rubric.description: Specifies that the electron arrangement is in shells around the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are arranged in shells around the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Electronic configuration is the distribution of electrons in the shells around the nucleus of an atom.

rubric.why: Mendeleev’s law describes a periodic repetition of element properties.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements are periodic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the properties of elements recur periodically.

rubric.why: Mendeleev arranged the elements according to their atomic masses.
rubric.description: Identifies atomic mass as the basis of the periodic relationship.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the periodicity is a function of atomic masses.

modelAnswer: Mendeleev’s Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses.

rubric.why: Lanthanides are the 14 elements following lanthanum, from cerium to lutetium.
rubric.description: Identifies the elements included among the lanthanides.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the series as the 14 elements from cerium to lutetium, following lanthanum.

rubric.why: The series is named for lanthanum and its members have similar properties.
rubric.description: Connects the series with lanthanum or identifies its periodic-table position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the elements resemble lanthanum or are the period-6 f-block series.

modelAnswer: Lanthanides are the 14 elements from cerium to lutetium that follow lanthanum in the periodic table.
They are called lanthanides because they have properties similar to lanthanum.

items.followUp: Why does ionization energy generally increase across a period?

rubric.why: Atomic size increases down a group, placing the outer electron farther from the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that atomic size or radius increases down the group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the increase in atomic size down a group.

rubric.why: Greater distance and shielding weaken the nucleus’s attraction to the outer electron, so less energy is needed to remove it.
rubric.description: Explains the weaker attraction and resulting decrease in ionization energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased distance or shielding to weaker attraction and less energy needed to remove the electron.

modelAnswer: Down a group, atomic size and the shielding effect increase.
The outer electron is farther from the nucleus and is less strongly attracted, so less energy is required to remove it.

items.followUp: Define a double covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond consists of one shared pair of electrons between two atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a single covalent bond in terms of sharing one electron pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two atoms share one pair of electrons.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates a single covalent bond.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of a single covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example such as H₂, HCl, or Cl₂.

modelAnswer: A single covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one pair of electrons.

items.followUp: Explain why hydrogen bonding occurs between water molecules.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding involves hydrogen covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom.
rubric.description: Identifies the hydrogen attached to an electronegative atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the hydrogen is covalently bonded to an electronegative atom such as oxygen, nitrogen, or fluorine.

rubric.why: The partially positive hydrogen is weakly attracted to an electronegative atom, commonly with a lone pair, on another molecule.
rubric.description: Describes the intermolecular attraction that constitutes hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that hydrogen is attracted to an electronegative atom on another molecule.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding is a weak intermolecular attraction between a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom, such as oxygen, nitrogen, or fluorine, and an electronegative atom in another molecule.
For example, it occurs between the hydrogen of one water molecule and the oxygen of another.
